items.headline: U.S. Futures Rebound Slightly After Thursday's Broad Market Decline
items.summary: U.S. stock futures showed modest gains this morning, attempting to recover from a significant sell-off on Thursday, August 20th. Yesterday's decline was driven by persistent concerns over rising Treasury yields, increasing crude oil prices, and a sharp drop in retail giant Walmart's shares following a disappointing earnings report. Geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran also contributed to market uncertainty.

items.headline: Coinbase Global ($COIN) Jumps on Regulatory News
items.summary: Coinbase Global ($COIN) rose 7.58% after President Trump reportedly advocated for the Clarity Act alongside crypto executives.

items.headline: Deere ($DE) Gains on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Deere ($DE) advanced 6.94% following a report of higher quarterly sales and earnings per share.

items.headline: Moderna ($MRNA) Falls as Vaccine Gains Reverse
items.summary: Moderna ($MRNA) plummeted 23.55% as previous gains from its cancer vaccine reversed after a sharp rally in the prior session.

items.headline: Walmart ($WMT) Continues Decline Post-Earnings
items.summary: Walmart Inc. ($WMT) dropped 9.15% after reporting its slowest domestic sales growth in six years and missing comparable sales expectations, with soft guidance hinting at a weakening consumer.

items.headline: FTAI Aviation ($FTAI) Slips Despite Financing News
items.summary: FTAI Aviation ($FTAI) declined 6.21% despite announcing a new $2 billion warehouse financing facility for aircraft acquisitions.

items.headline: Economic Data Shows Mixed Signals (Thursday, August 20, 2026)
items.summary: U.S. initial jobless claims decreased by 6,000 to 206,000 for the week ended August 15, marginally above the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 204,000. The Philadelphia Fed Index for August rose to 47.4, significantly beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 25 and July's 41.4. Leading Indicators increased 0.2% month-over-month in July, aligning with expectations.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Resume Upward Trend
items.summary: The benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield traded near 4.69% today, rising from Thursday's nearly 4.64%. The 30-year Treasury yield was approximately 5.24%. Yields resumed their upward trajectory despite the U.S. Treasury's plan to increase long-term debt buybacks, which initially offered temporary relief.

items.headline: Energy and Real Estate Lead, Consumer Sectors Lag (Thursday, August 20, 2026)
items.summary: On Thursday, nine out of eleven S&P 500 sectors closed in negative territory. Consumer Staples ($XLP), Health Care ($XLV), and Consumer Discretionary ($XLY) were among the weakest, falling 1.9%, 1.9%, and 1.8% respectively. Conversely, Energy Select Sector SPDR ($XLE) rose 0.4%, and Real Estate stocks also ended the session higher.

items.headline: Upcoming Economic Reports and Events
items.summary: Investors are awaiting reports on the S&P Global Manufacturing and Services PMI later today. No major earnings reports are scheduled for Friday. The highly anticipated Jackson Hole Economic Symposium is scheduled for August 27-29.
